No ready item = slot skipped, never filler. Final mp4s live in posting/ready/ (committed: they carry paid voice).

items.title: The 1% fee that eats 24% of your retirement
items.caption: 1% sounds like nothing. Over 40 years it quietly takes a quarter of your money. Here's the math.

items.title: A raise can't lower your pay (the tax bracket myth)
items.caption: Getting bumped into the 22% bracket doesn't put your whole paycheck at 22%. Only the dollars above the line. Here's the math on a $1,000 raise.

items.title: The minimum payment trap: $5,000, 19 years
items.caption: Pay only the minimum on a $5,000 card at 22% and it takes 19 years and $8,100 in interest. Keep paying that first payment instead and it's gone in under 5.

items.title: Lose 20%, gain 20%... you're still down
items.caption: $10,000 drops 20% to $8,000. A 20% gain only gets you to $9,600. You need 25% just to break even, and a 50% loss needs 100%.

items.title: The only instant 100% return (your 401k match)
items.caption: You put in $2,400, your employer adds $2,400. That's a 100% return on day one. Over 30 years, just the free half can grow to about $227K. Match terms and vesting vary.

items.title: When does your money double? Divide 72 by the rate
items.caption: At 8%, 72 ÷ 8 = 9 years to double. $10K becomes about $160K in 36 years. The same rule says a 24% credit card doubles your balance in about 3.

items.title: Your cash says $10,000. In 24 years it buys half.
items.caption: At 3% inflation, cash sitting at 0% loses half its buying power in about 24 years (72 ÷ 3). The number never changes. What it buys does.

items.title: Switching doors doubles your odds (it feels wrong)
items.caption: Three doors, one car. Switching wins 2 out of 3 times. Your gut says 50/50. Your gut is wrong.

items.title: Africa is 14x bigger than Greenland. Your map lied.
items.caption: On the map on your wall they look the same size. They are not even close.

items.title: Astronauts aren't weightless. They're falling.
items.caption: Gravity on the space station is about 90% of what you feel right now. So why do they float?

items.title: Multiply any number by 11 in your head
items.caption: No calculator, two seconds. Pause and try 72 x 11 first.

items.title: 23 people, 50% chance two share a birthday
items.caption: 365 days, only 23 people, and it's a coin flip. The trick: it's not 23 chances, it's 253 pairs. At 70 people it's 99.9%.

items.title: A million seconds is 11 days. A billion is 31 years.
items.caption: One letter apart, so your brain files them side by side. A billion seconds ago was early 1995. A trillion seconds ago, people were painting cave walls.

items.title: Buses every 10 minutes. Why do you wait 10, not 5?
items.caption: Long gaps catch more riders because they're long. Here 78% of riders land in the two long gaps, so the average wait is the full 10 minutes. Same reason classes feel bigger than the school says.

items.title: A 99% accurate test says you're sick. You're probably fine.
items.caption: Rare disease, 1 in 1,000. Test 1,000 people: 1 real positive, about 10 false alarms. So a positive means about a 9% chance. Test positive twice and it jumps to 91%. (Illustration, not medical advice.)
